Privacy

Information in contact, support and the paper workspace.

A short explanation of what Nortivo stores when you send an enquiry or use the private paper workspace.

What you send Services used Language and access The private paper workspace Sessions and retention Local testing and the hosted service

What you send

Forms send your name, email, subject and message to Nortivo’s ticket system. Your email is used for confirmation, access to the ticket and replies. Do not include passwords, payment card information or other sensitive details.

Services used

Netlify serves the website and server functions. Supabase stores tickets, replies and private paper workspaces in the hosted service. Resend sends contact and support email. This website has no added analytics or marketing tracking.

Language and access

Your selected language is saved in this browser. On your first visit, Netlify’s approximate country information may select Norwegian in Norway; otherwise English. We do not use GPS. Temporary cookies verify access to a support ticket or the admin area.

The private paper workspace

A guest receives a separate workspace without an email address. A registered paper account stores an email address, an optional name and a password stored as a secure hash rather than plain text. The workspace also stores watchlists, settings, strategy configuration, alerts, simulated orders, fills, ledger entries and technical events. Records are isolated between users and kept separate from Nortivo’s historical report.

Sessions and retention

A guest session cookie lasts one day. The guest workspace expires after seven days and is removed during later cleanup. A registered account session lasts seven days. The account and its paper history are retained until a separate deletion process is implemented. Email verification and password recovery are not currently connected to paper accounts.

Local testing and the hosted service

The developer’s local test version stores test accounts and paper records in a local SQLite database inside the project’s ignored .local folder. It does not connect to production Supabase, email, market-data or brokerage services. The local database is private but not encrypted. The hosted service uses server storage in Supabase. Passwords are not returned to the browser, and the session token is held in a restricted HttpOnly cookie that page scripts cannot read.

The small trading-rule illustration on the homepage uses fictional prices and neither stores nor sends anything. The full Trading Platform is different: private paper records are stored as described above.

Have a question about an enquiry, the paper workspace or your information? Create a support ticket.
